industries.name: Warehouse & Logistics
industries.intro: Inbound, storage and outbound are a chain of verification points. Every unrecorded exception travels with the inventory. These scenarios capture the physical truth before it reaches the WMS.

scenarios.title: Dock-to-stock receiving
scenarios.situation: Inbound pallets arrive mixed-SKU and often against a tight dock schedule. Manual counts drift from the ASN, shortages surface after put-away, and receiving data reaches the WMS late.
workflow: Scan the ASN and pallet license plate at the dock.
Verify carton count and SKU against the expected receipt.
Use UHF RFID for bulk pallet verification where tags are applied.
Flag short, over or unknown items and print an exception label on the spot.
Confirm receipt and release a put-away task to the WMS.
outcomes: Receiving discrepancies are caught at the dock, not after put-away.
Dock staff spend time moving goods instead of re-counting them.
WMS inventory reflects the floor within the receiving shift.
scenarios.note: Exception labeling uses a configured device with barcode capture or a compatible paired printer. Confirm media and print width for the SKU.

scenarios.title: RFID cycle counting
scenarios.situation: Cycle counts are planned around the cost of counting. Staff work shelf by shelf, counts are incomplete in dense storage, and different teams can reach different numbers for the same SKU.
workflow: Download the count plan and location list to the handheld.
Walk the aisles and capture UHF tags in bulk; scan barcodes for untagged items.
Review duplicates, exceptions and location mismatches on the device.
Run a blind recount for high-variance locations.
Post the count and variance report to WMS / ERP.
outcomes: More locations counted per shift with the existing team.
Consistent, audit-ready count records.
Faster identification of shrink and misplaced stock.

scenarios.title: Pick, pack and dispatch
scenarios.situation: Orders leave with the wrong item, quantity or label, and the error is discovered by the customer. Pack stations become a bottleneck when labels are printed somewhere else.
workflow: Scan the pick location and item against the order.
Verify quantity and serial or lot where required.
Pack to the carton and scan the carton ID.
Print the shipping label and packing document at the station.
Confirm dispatch and hand tracking data to the WMS / TMS.
outcomes: Order accuracy is verified before the parcel leaves.
Fewer trips and reprints between pack station and office printer.
Dispatch status is available to customer service in real time.
scenarios.note: Station printing requires a configured device or a compatible label printer.

industries.summary: Verify every unit at the dock, in the aisle and at dispatch — without adding a second counting step.
industries.valueLine: Catch receiving errors at the dock. Count the aisle in one pass. Ship the right parcel.

challenge.title: Inventory accuracy is decided at the point of work.
challenge.body: Most warehouse errors are not system errors. They are unrecorded physical exceptions: a short pallet, a mis-scanned pick, a label printed too late. The WMS can only be as accurate as the events it receives.
points: Receiving counts drift from the ASN, and shortages surface after put-away.
Cycle counts are planned around their cost, so problem locations are counted too late.
Pick, pack and labelling happen in different places, and errors reach the customer.
Exception data is written down or remembered instead of captured where it happens.

industries.name: Manufacturing
industries.intro: On the line, data is only useful when it is captured at the point of work. These scenarios connect materials, machines and people without adding another layer of paperwork.

scenarios.title: Work-order execution and WIP
scenarios.situation: Work orders are printed, signed and entered later. WIP status is a guess between stations, and scrap or rework is recorded after the fact.
workflow: Scan the work order and material at the first station.
Confirm routing and component consumption at each operation.
Capture pass, fail, scrap and rework codes at the station.
Scan the unit into the next operation or finished-goods area.
Post production confirmation to ERP / MES.
outcomes: WIP visibility between operations.
Production records captured at the point of work.
Scrap and rework traceable to the operation and operator.

scenarios.title: Material traceability and kitting
scenarios.situation: A quality issue triggers a search through paper records. Lot numbers are incomplete, and kitting errors are found only when the line stops.
workflow: Scan the kit list and each bin or component during kitting.
Validate lot, quantity and expiry against the work order.
Flag missing or wrong components before the kit leaves staging.
Scan the kit into the line and bind components to the work order.
Keep a component-to-unit record for quality and recall.
outcomes: Component-to-unit traceability without paper.
Kitting errors caught before a line stop.
Faster containment when a supplier lot is flagged.

scenarios.title: Equipment inspection rounds
scenarios.situation: Maintenance rounds are recorded on clipboards. Findings are transcribed later, and the same fault is rediscovered on the next shift.
workflow: Scan the asset tag at the machine.
Load the inspection checklist and record readings or conditions.
Capture photo evidence and flag out-of-tolerance values.
Raise a work request or spare-part requirement on the spot.
Sync completed rounds and findings to the CMMS / EAM.
outcomes: Inspection history tied to the asset, not to a clipboard.
Findings reach maintenance before the next shift.
Wired connection to legacy equipment where required.
scenarios.note: Connectivity and adapter requirements depend on the selected tablet configuration. Confirm the required ports and adapters before quotation.

industries.summary: Capture work orders, material consumption and quality events at the station, not after the shift.
industries.valueLine: Make every work order, kit and quality event traceable at the point of work.

industries.name: Retail & Commerce
industries.intro: Store teams are judged on availability and accuracy. The right capture tool shortens the gap between what the shelf shows and what the system believes.

scenarios.title: Replenishment and price accuracy
scenarios.situation: Shelf gaps are reported from memory, price labels drift from the POS, and backroom stock is invisible during a busy trading day.
workflow: Scan the shelf label or item to check price and stock.
Record shelf quantity and backroom availability.
Flag gaps and price mismatches for action.
Generate a replenishment or price-change task.
Sync counts to the store system.
outcomes: Shelf accuracy checked during normal store walks.
Price mismatches caught before the customer sees them.
Replenishment based on a counted shelf, not an estimate.

scenarios.title: RFID item-level stocktake
scenarios.situation: Stocktakes require extra staff and closed hours. Counts are incomplete in dense displays, and the same item is counted twice.
workflow: Load the store layout and count zones.
Sweep fixtures with UHF RFID; scan barcodes for untagged items.
Review duplicates and exceptions on the device.
Recount high-variance zones.
Post results to the merchandise system.
outcomes: Faster stocktakes with fewer staff hours.
Count records that can be audited.
A clearer view of shrinkage and misplaced stock.

scenarios.title: Mobile labeling and service
scenarios.situation: Staff leave the customer to find a label printer. Price changes and markdowns wait, and the customer experience suffers.
workflow: Scan the item to confirm identity and current price.
Select the required label or document template.
Print on the spot where the device is configured with a printer.
Attach the label and confirm the update.
Sync the price or markdown event to the POS.
outcomes: Labeling done at the point of decision.
Fewer trips to a back-office printer.
Price changes reflected consistently.
scenarios.note: Labeling workflows use a configured scanning device or a compatible paired printer. Confirm media and print width before deployment.

industries.summary: Keep shelf, backroom and price data aligned during the trading day, not after closing.
industries.valueLine: Know what is on the shelf, what is in the back room and what the label says — in one walk.

industries.name: Field Service & Asset Tracking
industries.intro: Field teams work where the network, the weather and the asset are all unpredictable. These scenarios keep records complete and assets visible.

scenarios.title: Inspection and digital work orders
scenarios.situation: Job sheets are completed on paper and keyed in at the end of the day. Photos are filed separately, and the office cannot see job status until the technician returns.
workflow: Receive the job and asset details on the device.
Scan the asset tag on arrival.
Complete the checklist, readings and photo evidence.
Capture the customer signature and close the job.
Sync the completed work order when connectivity is available.
outcomes: Job status visible while the technician is still on site.
Complete evidence attached to the asset record.
Less end-of-day administration.

scenarios.title: Asset tagging and audit rounds
scenarios.situation: Asset registers are out of date. Audits are annual events, and missing or moved assets are discovered late.
workflow: Load the asset list and audit scope.
Walk the site and capture UHF tags in bulk.
Scan close-range tags or barcodes where required.
Flag missing, moved or unknown assets.
Post the audit result to the asset system.
outcomes: Audits completed in hours, not days.
Missing assets identified at the point of audit.
The asset register maintained between formal audits.

scenarios.title: On-site service and documentation
scenarios.situation: A field engineer needs to label a repaired asset, print a service record or verify an identity document on site. Leaving to find equipment delays the visit.
workflow: Scan the asset and retrieve its service history.
Record parts used and work performed.
Print a service label or receipt where the configuration supports it.
Capture a signature or document reference where required.
Sync the record to the service platform.
outcomes: Service records completed during the visit.
On-site labeling and documentation.
Fewer return visits for missing paperwork.
scenarios.note: Document and identity capture requirements must be confirmed for the selected configuration and target region before deployment.

industries.summary: Complete the job record, asset audit and on-site documentation before the technician leaves.
industries.valueLine: Close the job on site, with the evidence attached to the asset.
